target_customer: Originally pharma partners and cancer patients (live biotherapeutics); now parents buying an infant and toddler synbiotic
problem: Gut microbes influence cancer treatment response and infant health, but few engineered microbiome therapies or evidence based infant products existed.
business_model: Preclinical microbiome therapeutics with study collaborations, plus direct to consumer subscription synbiotic for infants and toddlers

founders.name: Stephanie Culler
education: PhD (school and field not stated in opened sources)
founders.background_notes: Company site says she studied the microbiome for over a decade before founding the company.

founders.name: Steve Van Dien
education: PhD (school and field not stated in opened sources)
founders.background_notes: BioSpace (July 2022) describes both founders as synthetic and metabolic engineering pioneers; YC page lists him as Founder/CTO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering live gut bacteria into therapeutics requires synthetic biology, clinical trials and regulatory approval, which is research grade for a team of six.

defensibility.rationale: Strain data from the ARGONAUT and infant studies and patents could be hard to replicate, but no granted protection was confirmed in opened sources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired or copied it in sources found; larger microbiome firms such as Evelo and Seres existed but are not confirmed here with dated sources.

market_need_then: Research linking gut bacteria to cancer treatment response was reported during 2017 and 2018 per a search summary, but no dated source was opened.

branding.name_origin: Named for Persephone, the Greek goddess of renewal, per the Dieline packaging case study (Dec 2025).
branding.domain_note: Moved from persephonebiosciences.com to persephone.bio per the observed redirect; also persephonebiome.com in search results.

identity.visual_style: Pomegranate and berry reds with peach, custom bloom illustrations, serif headlines
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and science led: Bringing the gut microbiome back into bloom

branding.brand_signature: Bloom theme tying the Persephone myth to gut health
branding.community_and_virality: Dieline packaging feature and press logos on its site (Gizmodo, Scientific American, Axios per the site); no fan community evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: A coherent myth based brand for the consumer line with design press, but little public awareness evidence.

outcome_analysis: Persephone started in 2017 as a synthetic biology company targeting cancer through the gut microbiome and joined YC in Winter 2018. Its only verified round is a 15 million dollar seed in July 2022 co-led by First Bight Ventures and Propel Bio Partners, funding the ARGONAUT cancer study. It has since built a consumer infant synbiotic line backed by a clinical trial. Outcome remains open and it is still operating.
notes: Competitors left empty: pages that could date rivals such as Evelo and Seres returned 403 or 503 or were undated, so none is listed. Aggregators disagree on totals (15.1 million, 21.6 million) and one lists an April 2025 round; none verified, so only the July 2022 seed is recorded and a small early YC investment is not recorded as a round. A Caplight Series A headline appeared to belong to another company. The shift from cancer therapeutics to a consumer infant product is evidenced by the site and a trademark filing noted in a search summary (Nov 2024) but no source states a pivot date, so no pivot is recorded. No layoffs, acquisition or shutdown news found.
